standards_review.notes: git-workflow.md documents 'EPMCDME-####: Description'. 16 of 27 commits in range match exactly (e.g. 'EPMCDME-14855: Apply ruff formatting to tool-error cap test'). 7 commits insert a bracket tag between ticket and colon ('EPMCDME-14855 [F10]: tolerant chunk unpack + skip malformed streamed JSON', '[F9]', '[F7+F8]', '[F3]', '[F5+F6-REFRAME]', '[F2]', '[F1]'), and 2 use a lowercase non-ticket-prefixed subject ('epmcdme-14855-token-limit-slice2: add planning artifacts', 'epmcdme-14855-graph-cancellation-core: add planning artifacts'), none of which match the documented format. One merge commit subject is auto-generated by git and not authored to the convention.

Ruff-relevant style is clean: no Optional[]/bare list|dict found in the diff, new dict[...] annotations use modern generics (agent_streaming_callback.py), and all 3 new test files carry the Apache 2.0 header. One new method violates the guide's 'spell out the accepted union' rule for duck-typed parameters: _check_truncation_in_chunk(self, chunk) -> None at src/codemie/agents/langgraph_agent.py:1133 leaves chunk unannotated even though the body branches on its shape (tuple unpacking depends on self.subagents). It mirrors an existing unannotated sibling (_get_last_ai_message_content), but the guide's rule targets new code specifically.

Auth/authorization dependencies are untouched by this change. Secret handling: F2 (src/codemie/agents/langgraph_agent.py:842-847) fixes a real stacktrace-leak bug by redacting agent_error.stacktrace on error_response itself so get_error()/error_details no longer bypass HIDE_AGENT_STREAMING_EXCEPTIONS - this is a positive conformance to the 'never log/return sensitive values' rule, not a violation. Untrusted-input handling: F10's json.JSONDecodeError skip in _read_streamed_chunk (src/codemie/rest_api/handlers/assistant_handlers.py) is lenient rather than fail-closed, but the parsed value is the server's own internally-produced StreamedGenerationResult chunk read off an in-process queue, not externally-supplied/attacker-controlled input crossing a security boundary (the guide's own evidence, gitlab_webhook_security.py, is about external webhook bodies) - so this guide row does not extend to it. No credential logging, no injection, no auth-bypass pattern found in the changed files.

blocking_findings.location: commit subjects 'EPMCDME-14855 [F10]: ...', '[F9]', '[F7+F8]', '[F3]', '[F5+F6-REFRAME]', '[F2]', '[F1]', and 'epmcdme-14855-token-limit-slice2: add planning artifacts', 'epmcdme-14855-graph-cancellation-core: add planning artifacts'
blocking_findings.violation: git-workflow.md requires commit subjects in the form 'EPMCDME-####: Description'; these 9 commits either insert a bracket tag between the ticket and the colon or use a lowercase non-ticket-prefixed subject
blocking_findings.why_blocking: the documented commit-format standard is broken for roughly a third of the commits in the review range, which is a blocking standards violation per the review gate's own rule (partial blocks like fail)
blocking_findings.remedy: reword the affected subjects to drop the bracket tags (fold the [F#] label into the commit body instead of the subject) and prefix the two planning-artifact commits with the ticket in the documented 'EPMCDME-####: Description' form

blocking_findings.violation: code-quality.md's Types And Imports section requires spelling out the accepted union for a duck-typed parameter instead of leaving it unannotated; _check_truncation_in_chunk(self, chunk) -> None leaves chunk untyped even though the method's own body treats it as two different shapes depending on self.subagents
blocking_findings.why_blocking: a documented, blocking code-quality standard (explicit typing on new code) is unmet for this new method
blocking_findings.remedy: annotate chunk with the concrete accepted type/union (e.g. the same tuple/union already used by the sibling _get_last_ai_message_content) instead of leaving it bare
